title: Eruption of Thera
description: A huge volcanic eruption buries the Minoan town of Akrotiri; its exact date is debated.

title: First Olympic Games
description: By ancient reckoning the games in honour of Zeus are first held, and they continue every four years for a millennium.

title: Reforms of Cleisthenes
description: Cleisthenes reorganises the citizens of Athens and their council, the founding of Athenian democracy.

title: Battle of Marathon
description: The Athenians defeat the first Persian invasion of mainland Greece.

title: Battle of Thermopylae
description: Leonidas of Sparta and a small Greek force hold the pass against Xerxes' army for three days before being overwhelmed.

title: Battle of Salamis
description: The Greek fleet defeats the Persian fleet, and Xerxes withdraws most of his army.

title: Building of the Parthenon begins
description: Under Pericles the Athenians begin the temple of Athena on the Acropolis.

title: Peloponnesian War begins
description: Athens and Sparta and their allies begin a war that lasts 27 years and ends in Athens' defeat.

title: Trial and death of Socrates
description: An Athenian jury condemns the philosopher for impiety and corrupting the young, and he drinks hemlock.

title: Battle of Chaeronea
description: Philip II of Macedon defeats Athens and Thebes, ending the independence of the Greek city-states.

title: Alexander invades Asia
description: Alexander crosses the Hellespont and wins his first battle against the Persians.

title: Death of Alexander
description: Alexander dies at 32, and his generals divide the empire into kingdoms that spread Greek culture from Egypt to Central Asia.

title: Sack of Corinth
description: Rome destroys Corinth and brings Greece under its rule.

title: Constantinople dedicated
description: Constantine makes the Greek city of Byzantium his capital, the centre of the Greek-speaking Roman Empire for eleven centuries.

title: Hagia Sophia dedicated
description: Justinian's great domed church is completed after less than six years of building.

title: East–West Schism
description: Papal legates and the patriarch of Constantinople excommunicate each other, the conventional date of the split between the Catholic and Orthodox churches.

title: Battle of Manzikert
description: The Seljuks defeat and capture Emperor Romanos IV, and the Byzantines lose most of Anatolia.

title: War of Independence begins
description: By tradition Bishop Germanos raises the flag of revolt against Ottoman rule; fighting had started some days before.

title: Battle of Navarino
description: British, French and Russian ships destroy the Ottoman and Egyptian fleet, deciding the war in the Greeks' favour.

title: Independence recognised
description: The London Protocol of the three protecting powers declares Greece an independent state.

title: First modern Olympic Games
description: The revived games open in Athens.

title: Burning of Smyrna
description: A fire destroys the Greek and Armenian quarters days after the Turkish army retakes the city, the end of the Greek presence in Asia Minor.

title: Exchange of populations agreed
description: Greece and Turkey agree to a compulsory exchange that uproots about 1.2 million Orthodox Christians and 400,000 Muslims.

title: Greece rejects the Italian ultimatum
description: Greece refuses Mussolini's demands and then drives the invading Italian army back into Albania.

title: German invasion
description: Germany attacks Greece and occupies the mainland within a month; a harsh occupation and famine follow.

title: Civil War
description: Government forces backed by Britain and the United States defeat the communist Democratic Army.

title: Colonels' coup
description: Army officers seize power and rule as a junta for seven years.

title: Fall of the junta
description: After the crisis over Cyprus the military hands power to Konstantinos Karamanlis, and democracy is restored.

title: Greece joins the European Communities
description: Greece becomes the tenth member.

title: First bailout
description: Unable to borrow, Greece accepts loans from the euro area and the International Monetary Fund in return for austerity.
